title: Microstructure and Mechanism of Grain Raising in Wood
text: Microstructure and Mechanism of Grain Raising in Wood. Questions answered: Why does a sanded wood surface become rough again after wetting? Why are some wood species more prone to grain raising than others?. Why theme: 11. Product Function, Use and Performance (with secondary link to 10. Failure, Repair and Quality). title: Design and Assessment of Ergonomics of Hand Tools Based on Gender-Specific Operating Strategy: Two Case Studies on Shovels and Pruning Shears
text: Design and Assessment of Ergonomics of Hand Tools Based on Gender-Specific Operating Strategy: Two Case Studies on Shovels and Pruning Shears. Why theme: 7. Posture, Grip and Body Mechanics. Process stage: Sub-step 1.2: Extraction of Bamboo Root Questions answered Why is the labor-intensive digging and extraction of bamboo roots physically demanding, and how does shovel design affect musculoskeletal load?. Directly measures biomechanical and physiological load during shovel-based digging work, providing scientific grounding for the report's own description of root extraction as labor-intensive and time-consuming.

title: Combined Effects of Neem and Sesame Oil as a Wood Preservative on Subterranean Termites
text: Peer-reviewed field study (Maderas Ciencia y Tecnología) testing neem+sesame oil against termites on poplar; directly supports the 'why neem oil' Why-question.

title: Risk Factors Associated with Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders Among Floor-Sitting Precision Handicraft Workers
text: Risk Factors Associated with Work-Related Musculoskeletal Disorders Among Floor-Sitting Precision Handicraft Workers. Why theme: 7. Posture, Grip and Body Mechanics. Process stage: Detail carving (Nakshekari-equivalent fine work) and surface refinement Questions answered Why does prolonged seated precision carving work strain the back, neck and shoulders of bamboo root artisans?. Indian occupational study of floor-seated precision handicraft workers found high prevalence of neck, back and knee MSD symptoms linked to sustained posture during fine detail work, directly applicable to the sustained precision carving stages of bamboo root sculpture.

title: Wood Preservation Based on Neem Oil: Evaluation of Fungicidal and Termiticidal Effectiveness
text: Peer-reviewed study identifying neem's bioactive limonoid compounds and testing fungicidal/termiticidal effectiveness.

title: Adverse Health Manifestations in the Hands of Vibration Exposed Carpenters – A Cross Sectional Study
text: Adverse Health Manifestations in the Hands of Vibration Exposed Carpenters – A Cross Sectional Study. Why theme: 9. Vibration. Process stage: Initial cleaning, primary and secondary shaping (hammer + Battal) Questions answered Why does repeated hammer-driven chisel striking on dense bamboo root transmit harmful vibration to the artisan's hand?. Documents neural, vascular and musculoskeletal symptoms from repeated hand-tool impact vibration, directly relevant to the hammer-and-Battal striking method used throughout the report's rough and secondary shaping stages.

title: Effects of Neem Oil on the Preservation of Milicia excelsa
text: Peer-reviewed experimental study on a different (African) wood species; generalisable but not directly on Indian carving species — use cautiously.

title: Assessment of Dust Emission and Working Conditions in the Bamboo and Wooden Furniture Industries in Malaysia
text: Assessment of Dust Emission and Working Conditions in the Bamboo and Wooden Furniture Industries in Malaysia. Why theme: 8. Dust and Respiratory Exposure. Process stage: Sub-step 3.3: Sanding (Smoothing Stage) Questions answered Why does the sanding stage generate the highest dust emission and respiratory risk among bamboo craft workers?. This bamboo-industry-specific study found sanding operations produced the highest dust emission and associated respiratory ailments among workers, directly matching the report's two-stage sandpaper process (150 grit then 320 grit) as a key dust-generating step.

title: The Bio-Mechanical Properties of Coco Wood Applied with Neem Extracts
text: Peer-reviewed study also referencing neem-seed-oil-treated Bambusa vulgaris bamboo water-absorption/anti-swell properties.

title: Generation Rate and Particle Size Distribution of Wood Dust by Handheld Sanding Operation
text: Generation Rate and Particle Size Distribution of Wood Dust by Handheld Sanding Operation. Why theme: 8. Dust and Respiratory Exposure. Process stage: Sub-step 3.3: Sanding (Smoothing Stage) Questions answered Why does the choice of sandpaper grit (coarse 150 vs fine 320) affect the amount and particle size of dust generated during finishing?. Found that coarser sandpaper grits generate significantly more dust than finer grits, directly relevant to the report's two-stage sanding process moving from 150 grit (roughness removal) to 320 grit (smooth finishing).

title: Wood Carving Tools & Techniques for Beginners
text: General (non-Indian) woodworking video demonstrating tool selection and technique; useful HOW-layer comparison, not craft-specific.

title: Impulse Noise and Risk Criteria
text: Impulse Noise and Risk Criteria. Why theme: 8. Noise. Process stage: Initial cleaning, primary and secondary shaping (hammer + Battal) Questions answered Why does repeated hammer-on-chisel striking generate impulsive noise exposure that poses a distinct hearing risk from continuous noise?. This study specifically analyzes the sound pressure time function of chisel hammering as a model case of impulse noise, directly applicable to the repeated hammer-and-Battal striking method used across the bamboo root carving process's rough and secondary shaping stages.

title: I Spent 7 Days Learning the Craft of Wood Carving
text: Beginner-perspective video; anecdotal/hypothesis-level evidence only, illustrates common failure points.

title: A Review of Wood Machining Literature with a Special Focus on Sawing
text: A Review of Wood Machining Literature with a Special Focus on Sawing. Why theme: 6. Tools and Tool-Material Interaction. Process stage: Tool maintenance (ongoing, across all carving stages) Questions answered Why does regular sharpening of the Battal chisels reduce the physical effort required to carve dense bamboo root?. Confirms cutting force is inversely proportional to tool sharpness, explaining why the report identifies inconsistent access to quality sharpening stones (Selet Pathar, San Pathar) as a key tool maintenance challenge.

title: Lanolin as a Natural Agent for Improving Hydrophobicity and Biological Durability of Wood
text: Measures contact-angle increase (58 to 85-105 deg) from lanolin/wax finishing; relevant to natural preservation treatments used on carved wood.

title: Mechanical Properties of Bamboo Through Measurement of Culm Physical Properties for Composite Fabrication of Structural Concrete Reinforcement
text: Mechanical Properties of Bamboo Through Measurement of Culm Physical Properties for Composite Fabrication of Structural Concrete Reinforcement. Why theme: 6. Tools and Tool-Material Interaction. Process stage: Sub-step 1.1: Selection of Raw Material; all carving stages Questions answered Why does denser, more mature bamboo root require greater carving force and different chisel handling than less dense material?. Demonstrates that bamboo's specific density is directly correlated with its mechanical strength properties, supporting the report's own maturity-selection criteria (denser, heavier roots preferred) and explaining why mature bamboo root demands more carving force.

title: Superhydrophobic coatings on wood made of plant oil and natural wax
text: Explains mechanism by which tung oil and beeswax self-assemble into a hydrophobic surface layer; relevant to traditional oil/wax finishing.

title: The Decay Resistance and Hyphae Penetration of Bamboo Gigantochloa scortechinii Decayed by White and Brown Rot Fungi
text: The Decay Resistance and Hyphae Penetration of Bamboo Gigantochloa scortechinii Decayed by White and Brown Rot Fungi. Why theme: 10. Failure, Repair and Quality. Process stage: Sub-step 1.1: Selection of Raw Material Questions answered Why is immature bamboo more prone to cracking, decay and insect damage, making artisans avoid it in favor of mature roots?. Found that decay resistance to fungal rot increases significantly with bamboo age due to higher lignin, silica content and density in older culms, directly supporting the report's requirement that only mature bamboo root (minimum 3 years) be selected to avoid cracking, decay or insect damage.

title: Oil Heat Treatment of Wood - A Comprehensive Analysis of Physical, Chemical, and Mechanical Modifications
text: Comprehensive review of oil-heat treatment mechanisms and effect on wood's physical, chemical, mechanical properties and biological durability.

title: Improvement in Wood Bonding Strength of Poly (Vinyl Acetate-Butyl Acrylate) Emulsion by Controlling the Amount of Redox Initiator
text: Improvement in Wood Bonding Strength of Poly (Vinyl Acetate-Butyl Acrylate) Emulsion by Controlling the Amount of Redox Initiator. Why theme: 10. Failure, Repair and Quality. Process stage: Sub-step 3.4: Surface Treatment Questions answered Why does applying a Fevicol (PVA-based adhesive) and water mixture strengthen the bamboo root surface and seal its pores?. Studies how PVA-based emulsion adhesives penetrate and bond porous wood/fiber surfaces, providing a chemical basis for the report's own surface-treatment step of applying diluted Fevicol to strengthen and seal the bamboo root's surface pores before sun-drying.

title: Saharanpur's Heritage of Woodcraft: Prototyping a Future
text: Survey-based study of Saharanpur wood-carving cluster practice and market fit; useful for craft-integrity/product-performance context.

title: Exploring the Role of Task on Kinematic Variability and Assessing Consistency in Individual Responses Across Repetitive Manual Tasks
text: Exploring the Role of Task on Kinematic Variability and Assessing Consistency in Individual Responses Across Repetitive Manual Tasks. Why theme: 10. Quality (distinct from Failure). Process stage: Sub-step 3.1: Detail Carving (Fine Work) Questions answered Why is carving the eyes described as the most critical stage, and why does hand-controlled precision carving show natural variability between pieces?. Confirms motor variability is an inherent, measurable feature of human repetitive manual precision tasks, providing a scientific basis for why the report singles out eye-carving as the most critical and control-demanding stage of the entire process.

title: From Heritage to Luxury: Elevating Saharanpur's Wood Carving Craft to Global Luxury Markets
text: 2025 study on strategies to keep Saharanpur wood carving economically viable and craft-authentic while entering luxury markets.

title: Efficacy of Shellac-Based Varnishes for Protection of Wood Against Termite, Borer and Fungal Attack
text: Efficacy of Shellac-Based Varnishes for Protection of Wood Against Termite, Borer and Fungal Attack. Why theme: 11. Product Function, Use and Performance. Process stage: Sub-step 3.5: Final Finishing Questions answered Why would applying varnish to a finished bamboo root sculpture improve its protection and longevity beyond the natural finish?. An Indian Institute of Wood Science study found shellac-based varnishes gave up to 100% termite resistance for 6 months and improved fungal/borer resistance, supporting why varnish is offered as an optional protective final finish, while explaining why many artisans still prefer the natural unvarnished finish for aesthetic reasons.

title: Technique, Creativity, and Sustainability of Bamboo Craft Courses
text: Documents how bamboo/wood-carving courses balance hand skill with mechanical tools for sustainable skill transmission (Taiwan case study).

title: Densification of Bamboo: State of the Art
text: Densification of Bamboo: State of the Art. Why theme: 11. Product Function, Use and Performance. Process stage: Finished product (long-term use and care) Questions answered Why can a well-made bamboo root carving last over 50 years, and what material properties govern its long-term structural durability?. Reviews how bamboo's density, hardness and durability properties govern its long-term structural performance, providing scientific grounding for the report's claim that a well-made bamboo root carving can last over 50 years with proper care.

title: Wood Carving of Uttar Pradesh (Saharanpur)
text: Official craft encyclopedia entry naming Saharanpur's process sequence: slicing, carving, inlaying, sanding, polishing, assembling.

title: Drying and Control of Moisture Content and Dimensional Changes
text: Drying and Control of Moisture Content and Dimensional Changes. Why theme: 10. Failure, Repair and Quality. Process stage: Sub-step 3.4: Surface Treatment (sun-drying step) Questions answered Why must the bamboo root sculpture be sun-dried after surface treatment, and why could uneven drying introduce new cracking risk?. Explains that wood and lignocellulosic materials continuously exchange moisture with their environment and that uncontrolled or uneven drying leads to dimensional change and cracking, relevant to the report's sun-drying step following the Fevicol and water surface treatment. Applied here to bamboo root as a general lignocellulosic-material principle, not a bamboo-specific test.

title: WBC-2001
text: Orthogonal cutting mechanics of maple: Modeling a solid wood-cutting process. Questions answered: Why does cutting angle matter? Why does tool sharpness/rake angle matter? Why is a particular tool used for rough shaping?. Why theme: 6. Tools and tool-material interaction. Process stage: Cutting. Peer-reviewed force model for orthogonal wood cutting; shows cutting/thrust forces vary systematically with grain angle, rake angle and depth of cut. Lab milling setup, not hand-tool carving - mechanism transfers, exact force values do not.

title: WBC-2002
text: A review of wood machining literature with a special focus on sawing. Questions answered: Why does cutting along the grain differ from cutting across it? Why does tool sharpness matter? Why does cutting angle matter?. Why theme: 6. Tools and tool-material interaction. Process stage: Cutting. Peer-reviewed review consolidating decades of wood-machining studies: highest cutting forces occur cutting end grain (90-90), lowest cutting along the grain (90-0); wood density predicts force. Industrial sawing focus, a bridge between machine milling and hand-tool intuition.

title: WBC-2003
text: Effect of Grain Direction on Cutting Forces and Chip Geometry during Green Beech Wood Machining. Questions answered: Why is material cut in this direction? Why might the material tear rather than cut cleanly? Why does cutting angle matter?. Why theme: 4. Cutting, splitting and initial shaping. Process stage: Cutting. Peer-reviewed (BioResources) high-speed-imaging study: a 50-70 degree angle between cutting direction and grain gives the best compromise between low force and clean, non-splintering chips. Green (wet) beech tested; seasoned/dry carving wood may behave differently.

title: WBC-2004
text: A predictive model for the cutting force in wood machining developed using mechanical properties. Questions answered: Why does the artisan sometimes reverse cutting direction? Why is a particular tool used for rough shaping?. Why theme: 6. Tools and tool-material interaction. Process stage: Cutting. Links measurable wood mechanical properties (shear along grain, bending across grain) to predicted cutting force; a generalisable mechanism, not yet species-matched to the wood/bamboo items in this collection. Treat force numbers as indicative, not craft-specific.

title: WBC-2005
text: Machinability of Domestic Hardwoods (USDA data compilation). Questions answered: Why are some materials more suitable for fine carving? Why do certain tools affect the identity of the craft?. Why theme: 6. Tools and tool-material interaction. Process stage: Material. Digitised USDA machinability ratings (planing, shaping, turning, boring, sanding) by species; indicates which species machine/carve cleanly with hand tools versus which tear or chip. US species list - Indian wood/bamboo species not included, use only as a cross-check method template.

title: WBC-2006
text: Wood Handbook: Wood as an Engineering Material (Centennial/GTR-282 edition). Questions answered: Why does hardwood behave differently from soft wood in carving? Why does heartwood behave differently from sapwood? Why do knots increase difficulty or fracture risk?. Why theme: 1. Material selection. Process stage: Material. Authoritative USDA Forest Products Laboratory handbook; chapters on wood structure, machining and mechanical properties. CAM comprises software tools that translate digital designs (e.g., CAD-models) into machine-readable instructions (e.g., G-Code) for manufacturing, and is an integral part of digital fabrication. title: WBC-2016
text: Learning computer-aided manufacturing from demonstration: a case study with probabilistic movement primitives in robot wood carving. Questions answered: Why is a hand tool retained when a machine exists? Why must artisan control be preserved?. Why theme: 6. Tools and tool-material interaction. Process stage: Carving. Peer-reviewed robotics paper stating plainly that carving's tacit, hand-guided knowledge resists formalisation into standard CAM tool-paths, which is why hand-tool carving persists alongside automation - a plausible, evidence-informed hypothesis rather than settled craft doctrine.

title: WBC-2017
text: Sharpening Carving Chisels. Questions answered: Why this blade geometry? Why does sharpness change effort or surface finish?. Why theme: 6. Tools and tool-material interaction. Process stage: Carving. Practitioner guide stating carving chisels are double-bevelled at ~20 degrees (vs. ~25 degrees single-bevel cabinetmaker's chisels), which is why carving chisels cut cleanly at shallow angles without digging in - plausible craft rule, not independently tested here. Commercial tool-seller blog; treat the bevel angles as a starting figure to verify.

title: WBC-2018
text: Wood Carving of Saharanpur - Process: Carving. Questions answered: Why are holes drilled before final carving? Why is a pattern drawn, traced, templated or remembered? Why is a particular knife/chisel/file required?. Why theme: 5. Fine carving, piercing and decorative work. Process stage: Carving. D'Source case study of Saharanpur's sheesham-wood carvers: pattern is pasted on as paper, holes drilled first to remove negative space quickly, then hand tools (saw, plane, hard stone, chisels) finish the relief.

title: WBC-2019
text: Udayagiri Wooden Cutlery - official craft/tool profile. Questions answered: Why is this tool used at this stage? Why is a softer/harder/heavier/lighter material preferred? Why is a hand tool retained when a machine exists?. Why theme: 6. Tools and tool-material interaction. Process stage: Preparation. Office of the Development Commissioner (Handicrafts) profile of the exact reference craft named in the Protocol: names the specific tools (goruli/uli chisels, golkaadi files, rampam saw, sutti hammer, badisa axe) and confirms softwood vs hardwood use by product size, with hand tools dominant and only a paper-finishing machine for large pieces.

title: WBC-2020
text: IIT Kharagpur to Host First Craft Toolkit Workshop 'Srishti O Anusandhan' (with DC Handicrafts). Questions answered: Why is this tool used at this stage? Why must artisan control be preserved? Why does tool affordability matter?. Why theme: 6. Tools and tool-material interaction. Process stage: Other. News coverage of the DCH Centre of Excellence's first toolkit workshop, convening Udayagiri, Saharanpur, Odisha wood-carving, Kallakurichi (GI) and NE Cane & Bamboo artisans at IIT Kharagpur to document tools and materials directly with the artisans.

title: WBC-2021
text: The Mechanics of Splitting Wood and the Design of Neolithic Woodworking Tools. Questions answered: Why is splitting sometimes preferred to sawing? Why does cutting angle matter? Why this blade geometry (wedge)?. Why theme: 4. Cutting, splitting and initial shaping. Process stage: Cutting. Peer-reviewed experimental mechanics: splitting force rises with wedge angle (a shallower wedge splits more easily but travels less predictably); wood resists tangential splitting more than radial splitting, explaining traditional wedge/axe design choices.

title: WBC-2022
text: High Speed Steel Tool Wear After Wood Milling in the Presence of High Temperature Tribochemical Reactions. Questions answered: Why does material cost differ (tool wear/replacement)? Why does tool sharpness matter? Why do certain tools affect the identity of the craft?. Why theme: 6. Tools and tool-material interaction. Process stage: Cutting. Peer-reviewed study showing some wood species dull steel edges unusually fast via high-temperature tribochemical reactions (not just abrasive mineral content) - a documented, non-obvious reason certain species are harder on tools/require more frequent resharpening.

title: WBC-2023
text: Properties of potential wood carving species in Kenya. Questions answered: Why are some materials more suitable for fine carving? Why does material cost differ? Why might substitute materials alter quality or identity?. Why theme: 1. Material selection. Process stage: Material. Peer-reviewed comparison of conventional vs potential carving-wood species: density and hardness correlate strongly, higher density improves carved-surface quality but demands sharper tools; colour is a separate, non-mechanical selection criterion. Kenyan species, not Indian - use for the density-hardness-sharpness relationship only.

title: WBC-2024
text: Influence of basic wood density on the specific cutting energy. Questions answered: Why is a softer/harder/heavier/lighter material preferred? Why does tool sharpness change effort? Why is a particular tool used for rough shaping?. Why theme: 6. Tools and tool-material interaction. Process stage: Cutting. Peer-reviewed study modelling specific cutting energy (effort per unit of wood removed) as a function of basic wood density, consolidating multiple prior wood-machining force studies - a quantitative basis for why denser species need more cutting effort/sharper tools. Brazilian species tested; density-energy relationship transferable, not the specific numbers.

title: WBC-2025
text: Investigation of the Surface Quality and Tool Wear When Forming the Edges of Wood Materials. Questions answered: Why does sharpness change effort or surface finish? Why does cutting angle matter? Why is excess material retained initially?. Why theme: 6. Tools and tool-material interaction. Process stage: Cutting. Peer-reviewed finding that a smaller sharpening/oblique angle on the cutting edge reduces surface hairiness/roughness, and that as the edge dulls, surface irregularities first increase then appear to (deceptively) smooth out as the blunt edge crushes rather than cuts fibres. Engineered wood-panel context, not solid carving wood.

title: WBC-2026
text: Optimal cylindrical handle diameter for grip force tasks. Questions answered: Why this handle length/diameter? Why is a certain grip necessary? Why can a support/jig reduce effort?. Why theme: 6. Tools and tool-material interaction. Process stage: Other. Peer-reviewed grip-force study finding an optimal cylindrical handle diameter of about 19.7% of the user's hand length for maximum grip-force capability - a concrete, testable basis for why chisel/knife/dao handle diameter is not arbitrary. Laboratory grip-force study, not a wood/bamboo tool study specifically.

title: WBC-2027
text: An Ergonomics Guide to Hand Tools (handle diameter vs. torque model). Questions answered: Why this handle length/diameter? Why does tool-handle diameter affect effort?. Why theme: 6. Tools and tool-material interaction. Process stage: Other. Analytical/experimental model (Replogle) showing maximum hand torque on a cylindrical handle increases with the square of handle diameter up to a 'grip-span diameter' of about 2.5 cm, beyond which torque capacity falls - explains why very thin or very thick handles both reduce control. Generic ergonomics model; treat the 2.5 cm figure as indicative only.

title: WBC-2028
text: Roughness of Sanded Wood Surface: an Impact of Wood Species, Grain Direction and Grit Size of Abrasive Material. Questions answered: Why are different files/abrasives used sequentially? Why does finishing affect colour, texture or gloss? Why does surface smoothness matter?. Why theme: 6. Tools and tool-material interaction. Process stage: Finishing. Peer-reviewed, 1800-measurement study: surface roughness decreases as abrasive grit number increases (80 to 220), and roughness also depends on wood species and grain-cutting direction - the quantitative basis for why sanding is done in stages of increasing grit. Temperate species tested on an eccentric sanding stand; grit-vs-roughness relationship transferable.

title: WBC-2029
text: Analysis of the parameters affecting the surface sanding of Pinus elliottii and Corymbia citriodora wood species. Questions answered: Why are different files/abrasives used sequentially? Why does finish quality depend on the abrasive, not just the wood?. Why theme: 6. Tools and tool-material interaction. Process stage: Finishing. Peer-reviewed finding that sandpaper grit size and abrasive type (aluminium oxide gave a better, longer-lasting finish than silicon carbide) drove roughness and material-removal rate far more than wood species or fibre direction did. Two specific species tested; the abrasive-type/grit dominance finding is transferable.

title: WBC-2030
text: Wedge splitting test of wood for fracture parameters estimation of Norway Spruce. Questions answered: Why does material crack? Why does a carved bridge/thin section break?. Why theme: 4. Cutting, splitting and initial shaping. Process stage: Cutting. Peer-reviewed digital-image-correlation study of how a wedge-splitting crack initiates and propagates through spruce wood, giving a measurable fracture-energy basis for why splitting proceeds along the fibre once started rather than tearing sideways. Laboratory fracture-mechanics testing, not a craft-tool study.

title: WBC-2031
text: Bamboo Basketry - Bengaluru: Tools and Raw Materials. Questions answered: Why is this tool used at this stage? Why is a particular knife/chisel/file required? Why is water used before working the material?. Why theme: 6. Tools and tool-material interaction. Process stage: Preparation. D'Source documentation assigning a distinct role to each tool in the kit - big knife for peeling skin before soaking, small knife for trimming, hacksaw for sizing, chisel for smoothing the peeled surface - a directly observed division of labour among tools.

title: WBC-2032
text: Bamboo Mat Weaving - Tripura: Tools and Raw Materials. Questions answered: Why is a particular tool used for rough shaping? Why is splitting sometimes preferred to sawing?. Why theme: 4. Cutting, splitting and initial shaping. Process stage: Preparation. D'Source documentation distinguishing a big knife (slicing) from a small knife (trimming extra sticks) as separate tools for splitting/cutting/slicing bamboo strips for mat weaving - directly observed tool differentiation by task.
